lines.text: Many of the Jews who had seen what Jesus did believed in Him, but some went to the Pharisees.
The chief priests and Pharisees convened the Sanhedrin and feared that the Greeks would take away their place and nation.
Caiaphas, high priest that year, prophesied Jesus would die for the nation and gather God's scattered children into one.
The council plotted to kill Jesus, so He withdrew to a town called Emmaus and stayed there with the disciples.
As Passover neared, the chief priests and Pharisees ordered that anyone who knew where Jesus was must report it.
